MCP client configuration formats — important quirks:

CLAUDE CODE (~/.claude.json or via `claude mcp add`):
- Format: {"type": "http", "url": "http://...:port/mcp", "headers": {...optional}}
- Type can be: "http", "sse", "stdio"
- "http" = streamable HTTP (modern, recommended)
- DO NOT put mcpServers in ~/.claude/settings.json — that's deprecated, use ~/.claude.json
- CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> -s user` (user scope = global)
- Tool list cached at session start — restart Claude Code with /exit if backend changes

CLAUDE DESKTOP (claude_desktop_config.json):
- Only accepts stdio servers in claude_desktop_config.json (command + args format)
- Remote HTTP/SSE servers MUST be added via GUI: Settings → Connectors → Custom Connector
- Adding remote HTTP entries to the JSON file gets rejected as "not valid mcp servers"
- Claude Desktop also REQUIRES HTTPS for remote connectors (HTTP is rejected)
- Use the mcp-https gateway with valid wildcard cert

CURSOR/WINDSURF:
- Format: {"serverUrl": "http://..."} (note: serverUrl not url)

PROTOCOL NOTES:
- Streamable HTTP endpoint convention: /mcp (POST + GET)
- Initialize handshake: POST /mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, body has method=initialize
- Stateless mode (--stateless on mcp-proxy) means no session_id needed — each request independent
- SSE transport (deprecated) uses /sse endpoint, has session_id, breaks on backend restart
- After mcp-proxy 0.x updates: --sse-port renamed to --port, --sse-host to --host

     mcp-<name>:
       build: .

       network_mode: host
       restart: unless-stopped

         - com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=false

7. Add to Claude Code config: claude mcp add --transport http <name> http://192.168.178.2:<port>/mcp -s user
8. Add HTTPS route in /shared/config/mcp-https/conf/nginx.conf:

MCP client configuration formats — important quirks:

CLAUDE CODE (~/.claude.json or via `claude mcp add`):
- Format: {"type": "http", "url": "http://...:port/mcp", "headers": {...optional}}
- Type can be: "http", "sse", "stdio"
- "http" = streamable HTTP (modern, recommended)
- DO NOT put mcpServers in ~/.claude/settings.json — that's deprecated, use ~/.claude.json
- CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> -s user` (user scope = global)
- Tool list cached at session start — restart Claude Code with /exit if backend changes

CLAUDE DESKTOP (claude_desktop_config.json):
- Only accepts stdio servers in claude_desktop_config.json (command + args format)
- Remote HTTP/SSE servers MUST be added via GUI: Settings → Connectors → Custom Connector
- Adding remote HTTP entries to the JSON file gets rejected as "not valid mcp servers"
- Claude Desktop also REQUIRES HTTPS for remote connectors (HTTP is rejected)
- Use the mcp-https gateway with valid wildcard cert

CURSOR/WINDSURF:
- Format: {"serverUrl": "http://..."} (note: serverUrl not url)

PROTOCOL NOTES:
- Streamable HTTP endpoint convention: /mcp (POST + GET)
- Initialize handshake: POST /mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, body has method=initialize
- Stateless mode (--stateless on mcp-proxy) means no session_id needed — each request independent
- SSE transport (deprecated) uses /sse endpoint, has session_id, breaks on backend restart
- After mcp-proxy 0.x updates: --sse-port renamed to --port, --sse-host to --host

MCP servers architecture on solidPC (2026-04 setup):

- All MCP servers run as Docker containers on solidPC (192.168.178.2)
- Each server uses mcp-proxy (ghcr.io/sparfenyuk/mcp-proxy) to wrap a stdio MCP backend and expose Streamable HTTP at /mcp endpoint
- CRITICAL: must use --stateless flag for proper multi-client support (SSE is deprecated in MCP spec)
- All containers use network_mode: host to avoid Docker network pool exhaustion
- Configs at /shared/config/mcp-<name>/

why we chose stdlib-only http MCP client:
MCP client configuration formats — important quirks:

CLAUDE CODE (~/.claude.json or via `claude mcp add`):
- Format: {"type": "http", "url": "http://...:port/mcp", "headers": {...optional}}
- Type can be: "http", "sse", "stdio"
- "http" = streamable HTTP (modern, recommended)
- DO NOT put mcpServers in ~/.claude/settings.json — that's deprecated, use ~/.claude.json
- CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> -s user` (user scope = global)
- Tool list cached at session start — restart Claude Code with /exit if backend changes

CLAUDE DESKTOP (claude_desktop_config.json):
- Only accepts stdio servers in claude_desktop_config.json (command + args format)
- Remote HTTP/SSE servers MUST be added via GUI: Settings → Connectors → Custom Connector
- Adding remote HTTP entries to the JSON file gets rejected as "not valid mcp servers"
- Claude Desktop also REQUIRES HTTPS for remote connectors (HTTP is rejected)
- Use the mcp-https gateway with valid wildcard cert

CURSOR/WINDSURF:
- Format: {"serverUrl": "http://..."} (note: serverUrl not url)

PROTOCOL NOTES:
- Streamable HTTP endpoint convention: /mcp (POST + GET)
- Initialize handshake: POST /mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, body has method=initialize
- Stateless mode (--stateless on mcp-proxy) means no session_id needed — each request independent
- SSE transport (deprecated) uses /sse endpoint, has session_id, breaks on backend restart
- After mcp-proxy 0.x updates: --sse-port renamed to --port, --sse-host to --host

Claude Desktop with remote HTTP MCP servers — the correct approach (2026-04):

Claude Desktop's claude_desktop_config.json ONLY supports stdio servers (command + args). The "Custom Connector" GUI for remote servers requires cloud OAuth authorization which fails for local/LAN URLs. Direct HTTP/SSE entries in the JSON file are rejected as invalid.

SOLUTION: Use mcp-remote (npm package by geelen) as a stdio→HTTP bridge. Each MCP server entry runs `npx mcp-remote <url>` which spawns a stdio process locally that proxies all calls to the remote HTTP MCP server.

EXAMPLE config for claude_desktop_config.json:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "qdrant": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote",
        "http://192.168.178.2:32775/mcp",
        "--allow-http",
        "--transport",
        "http-only"
      ]
    }
  }
}

KEY FLAGS:
- --allow-http: required for non-HTTPS URLs (default rejects http:// for security)
- --transport http-only: skip SSE fallback, force streamable HTTP
- -y on npx: auto-install package without prompting
- mcp-remote also handles OAuth automatically when needed (stores tokens locally)

This means the HTTPS gateway (mcp-https on port 8443) is NOT needed for Claude Desktop. The plain HTTP MCP endpoints (32769-32776) work directly via mcp-remote.

Requires Node.js installed on the Claude Desktop machine (npx/npm).

MCP client configuration formats — important quirks:

CLAUDE CODE (~/.claude.json or via `claude mcp add`):
- Format: {"type": "http", "url": "http://...:port/mcp", "headers": {...optional}}
- Type can be: "http", "sse", "stdio"
- "http" = streamable HTTP (modern, recommended)
- DO NOT put mcpServers in ~/.claude/settings.json — that's deprecated, use ~/.claude.json
- CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> -s user` (user scope = global)
- Tool list cached at session start — restart Claude Code with /exit if backend changes

CLAUDE DESKTOP (claude_desktop_config.json):
- Only accepts stdio servers in claude_desktop_config.json (command + args format)
- Remote HTTP/SSE servers MUST be added via GUI: Settings → Connectors → Custom Connector
- Adding remote HTTP entries to the JSON file gets rejected as "not valid mcp servers"
- Claude Desktop also REQUIRES HTTPS for remote connectors (HTTP is rejected)
- Use the mcp-https gateway with valid wildcard cert

CURSOR/WINDSURF:
- Format: {"serverUrl": "http://..."} (note: serverUrl not url)

PROTOCOL NOTES:
- Streamable HTTP endpoint convention: /mcp (POST + GET)
- Initialize handshake: POST /mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, body has method=initialize
- Stateless mode (--stateless on mcp-proxy) means no session_id needed — each request independent
- SSE transport (deprecated) uses /sse endpoint, has session_id, breaks on backend restart
- After mcp-proxy 0.x updates: --sse-port renamed to --port, --sse-host to --host

DOCKERFILE PATTERN for new mcp-proxy-based server:
FROM ghcr.io/sparfenyuk/mcp-proxy:latest
RUN apk add --no-cache nodejs npm && npm install -g <pkg>  # for Node servers

- mcp-proxy base image is Alpine with Python 3.13 — use apk not apt, install node via apk

- The mcp-proxy --port 0 (--sse-port deprecated alias) means random port, must specify
- For env vars to pass to subprocess, use --pass-environment flag
- Command-line args after -- go to the wrapped server
- Some servers need full source not pip package (e.g. arr-suite-mcp has broken pyproject.toml, need git clone + manual cp -r to site-packages)

- Path-based routing: https://mcp.mannixbase.duckdns.org:8443/<service>/mcp
- nginx config requires: proxy_buffering off, proxy_request_buffering off, proxy_http_version 1.1, long timeouts (86400s), chunked_transfer_encoding on
- LAN-only via allow 192.168.178.0/24; deny all

MCP client configuration formats — important quirks:

CLAUDE CODE (~/.claude.json or via `claude mcp add`):
- Format: {"type": "http", "url": "http://...:port/mcp", "headers": {...optional}}
- Type can be: "http", "sse", "stdio"
- "http" = streamable HTTP (modern, recommended)
- DO NOT put mcpServers in ~/.claude/settings.json — that's deprecated, use ~/.claude.json
- CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> -s user` (user scope = global)
- Tool list cached at session start — restart Claude Code with /exit if backend changes

CLAUDE DESKTOP (claude_desktop_config.json):
- Only accepts stdio servers in claude_desktop_config.json (command + args format)
- Remote HTTP/SSE servers MUST be added via GUI: Settings → Connectors → Custom Connector
- Adding remote HTTP entries to the JSON file gets rejected as "not valid mcp servers"
- Claude Desktop also REQUIRES HTTPS for remote connectors (HTTP is rejected)
- Use the mcp-https gateway with valid wildcard cert

CURSOR/WINDSURF:
- Format: {"serverUrl": "http://..."} (note: serverUrl not url)

PROTOCOL NOTES:
- Streamable HTTP endpoint convention: /mcp (POST + GET)
- Initialize handshake: POST /mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, body has method=initialize
- Stateless mode (--stateless on mcp-proxy) means no session_id needed — each request independent
- SSE transport (deprecated) uses /sse endpoint, has session_id, breaks on backend restart
- After mcp-proxy 0.x updates: --sse-port renamed to --port, --sse-host to --host

MCP client configuration formats — important quirks:

CLAUDE CODE (~/.claude.json or via `claude mcp add`):
- Format: {"type": "http", "url": "http://...:port/mcp", "headers": {...optional}}
- Type can be: "http", "sse", "stdio"
- "http" = streamable HTTP (modern, recommended)
- DO NOT put mcpServers in ~/.claude/settings.json — that's deprecated, use ~/.claude.json
- CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> -s user` (user scope = global)
- Tool list cached at session start — restart Claude Code with /exit if backend changes

CLAUDE DESKTOP (claude_desktop_config.json):
- Only accepts stdio servers in claude_desktop_config.json (command + args format)
- Remote HTTP/SSE servers MUST be added via GUI: Settings → Connectors → Custom Connector
- Adding remote HTTP entries to the JSON file gets rejected as "not valid mcp servers"
- Claude Desktop also REQUIRES HTTPS for remote connectors (HTTP is rejected)
- Use the mcp-https gateway with valid wildcard cert

CURSOR/WINDSURF:
- Format: {"serverUrl": "http://..."} (note: serverUrl not url)

PROTOCOL NOTES:
- Streamable HTTP endpoint convention: /mcp (POST + GET)
- Initialize handshake: POST /mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, body has method=initialize
- Stateless mode (--stateless on mcp-proxy) means no session_id needed — each request independent
- SSE transport (deprecated) uses /sse endpoint, has session_id, breaks on backend restart
- After mcp-proxy 0.x updates: --sse-port renamed to --port, --sse-host to --host

Claude Desktop with remote HTTP MCP servers — the correct approach (2026-04):

Claude Desktop's claude_desktop_config.json ONLY supports stdio servers (command + args). The "Custom Connector" GUI for remote servers requires cloud OAuth authorization which fails for local/LAN URLs. Direct HTTP/SSE entries in the JSON file are rejected as invalid.

SOLUTION: Use mcp-remote (npm package by geelen) as a stdio→HTTP bridge. Each MCP server entry runs `npx mcp-remote <url>` which spawns a stdio process locally that proxies all calls to the remote HTTP MCP server.

EXAMPLE config for claude_desktop_config.json:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "qdrant": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote",
        "http://192.168.178.2:32775/mcp",
        "--allow-http",
        "--transport",
        "http-only"
      ]
    }
  }
}

KEY FLAGS:
- --allow-http: required for non-HTTPS URLs (default rejects http:// for security)
- --transport http-only: skip SSE fallback, force streamable HTTP
- -y on npx: auto-install package without prompting
- mcp-remote also handles OAuth automatically when needed (stores tokens locally)

This means the HTTPS gateway (mcp-https on port 8443) is NOT needed for Claude Desktop. The plain HTTP MCP endpoints (32769-32776) work directly via mcp-remote.

FROM ghcr.io/sparfenyuk/mcp-proxy:latest

For CD-Q4_K_M: Layer 0 (highest importance) gets Q5_K, Layers 1-6,10 (medium) get Q4_K, Layers 7-29 (lower) get Q3_K, output/embeddings get Q8_0. Uses llama-quantize --tensor-type-file with per-tensor type mapping. Tensor type files use format "blk.0.attn_q.weight=Q5_K" (= separator, no comments). Similar to Unsloth UD approach but using our own profiling data. Successfully created CD-Q6_K, CD-Q5_K_M, CD-Q4_K_M, CD-Q3_K_M quants, all passed sanity check.

osync project overview: CLI tool for managing Ollama models across local and remote servers. Written in C# targeting .NET 8 (net8.0-windows10.0.22621.0). Repository at https://github.com/mann1x/osync on pandorum at C:\Users\manni\source\repos\osync. Tests use SpecFlow + xUnit. Key commands: cp (copy models), ls (list), rm (remove), mv (rename), update, pull, show, run/chat, ps, psmonitor (real-time GPU/system monitor), load/unload (VRAM management), manage (full-screen TUI), qc (quantization comparison), qcview (QC results viewer), bench (context tracking benchmark), benchview (bench results viewer), install, showversion. Build: dotnet build / dotnet publish -c Release. Run from: .\osync\bin\Debug\net8.0-windows10.0.22621.0\osync.exe. NEVER save generated files in the repo directory (pushed to GitHub) — use .\osync\bin as working directory.

transformers device_map offloading: device_map="auto" with max_memory is INFERENCE ONLY — accelerate dispatch hooks don't support backward pass (gradients). For training/Fisher/backward: load model on CPU (device_map="cpu"), move individual layers to GPU one at a time. Also: device_map="auto" calls get_balanced_memory() which can override max_memory — use device_map="sequential" if you need max_memory respected for inference. The key in max_memory must be integer 0, not string "0".
